scope: Theorem 3.1 (Uniform transfer) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a constant C < ∞ with the following property. For each a > 0, all sufficiently large fixed integers L admit an integer s0, linear functionals ℓs : Xs → R, and vectors es ∈ Xs, for every integer s ≥ s0, such that ∥ℓs∥ ≤ C, ∥es∥q ≤ C, ℓs(es) = 1, (3.3) ∥Asf∥q ≤ CL|ℓs(f)| + a ∥f∥q , (3.4) |ℓLs(Asf) − Lℓs(f)| ≤ a ∥f∥q . (3.5) The constant C is independent of a, L, s. The choices are made in the following order: first L, then a larger fixed measurement ratio H, then the approximation accuracies used below, and finally s0. In particular, all estimates hold simultaneously for all s ≥ s0 and all bounded functions in Xs.
